inspector.modality: Native MRI and categorical temporal/ventricular source boundaries
inspector.title: Temporal and ventricular context in original SPL MRI
inspector.caption: Inspect 18 selected source classes for temporal and periventricular context, including paired lateral ventricular spaces, temporal horns, whole source white matter and selected temporal parcels. Native T1/T2, source-label overlays and original categorical-cell boundaries share the declared source affines. Ventricular-wall layers, complete sulcal/grey–white anatomy, hippocampal subdivisions and migration/dysplastic lesions remain unverified or absent. Other source relationship groups remain available; their presence grants no complete reporting coverage.

context_group.title: Temporal and ventricular source context
context_group.activity: Compare lateral ventricular spaces and temporal horns, adjacent source white matter and selected temporal parcels in native T1/T2 and exact categorical-cell boundaries. Start with the left and right lateral ventricular classes, then choose a source class or retained component and inspect all three native planes.
missing_or_unresolved_structures: Ventricular classes depict source-labelled spaces, not separately segmented ependymal or ventricular-wall layers.
Temporal-pole classes do not segment the adjacent middle-cranial-fossa floor or demonstrate an encephalocele/skull-base defect.
The selected temporal parcels are not the complete cortex, cortical ribbon or fine hippocampal head/body/tail architecture.
Source gyral labels do not delineate separately acquired sulcal curves or every grey–white biological boundary.
Heterotopia, focal cortical dysplasia and transmantle lesions are not supplied or validated by these reference labels.
The same-source limbic and separate fine-architecture references retain their own subject, registration and label-granularity limits.
semantic_limits: A whole source white-matter class supplies spatial context, not tract connectivity or a validated cortex-to-ventricle lesion path.
No normal-population range, current-patient registration, diagnostic accuracy or complete epilepsy reporting coverage is established.
